advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Handle non-OK responses in the Effective Policy fetch (check `r.ok` / map an errors payload to the unavailable banner) so a 403/500 is not rendered as an empty policy.
evidence: rebarProvider.jsx:1792 `.then((r) => r.json())` with no `r.ok` guard before parsing
rebarProvider.jsx:1761 `if (view.available === false)` — only an `available:false` shape triggers the unavailable banner; a 403 error body has neither `available` nor `criteria`
editor_server.py:238 the endpoint returns 403 `{"errors":[...]}` when `_authed()` is false
advisory.finding: The Effective Policy fetch in the JSX does not check `r.ok`; because `fetch` does not reject on HTTP error status, a 403 (missing/bad token) response body `{"errors":[...]}` is parsed and stored as `view`, and `formatEffectivePolicy` then renders it as an empty policy (digest `(none)`, `(no criteria)`) instead of the intended unavailable/error banner.
scenarios: Token drift or a stale host page causes /effective-policy to return 403; the panel shows a blank 'digest: (none) / (no criteria)' view rather than surfacing that the view is unavailable.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure the criterion-authoring path supplies `gate` (and an `applies_to` selector) to `validate_criterion_authoring`, or derive the gate independently, so the AC3 guard is reachable from the real editor rather than only from hand-crafted test routing.
evidence: editor_server.py:382 `errors = editor_contracts.validate_criterion_authoring(pid, routing)` with `routing = data.get("routing")` (no gate injected)
rebarProvider.jsx:1170 the built routing is `{ exec, applies_at, block_threshold, default_posture }` — no `gate` and no `applies_to` key
rebarProvider.jsx:1338 comment `A plan-review criterion carries its ROUTING overlay` — the UI only authors plan-review-shaped routing
search for `gate` in rebarProvider.jsx returns only label text (1262) and the read-only view (1772); nothing sets routing.gate
blocking.finding: The fail-loud authoring guard `validate_criterion_authoring` gates on `routing.get("gate") != _CODE_GATE`, but the editor's JSX `buildRouting()` never emits a `gate` key (nor an `applies_to` field) in the routing it POSTs to /library/create. So for every criterion authored through the real editor UI the guard short-circuits to `[]` and RP-06 AC3 is never enforced end-to-end — the enforcement is exercised only by unit tests that hand-craft a routing dict containing `gate: "code_review"`.
scenarios: A user authors a project.* code-review criterion through the editor with empty/blank applies_to — the guard is skipped because routing has no gate key, so the invalid criterion is written instead of being refused with the located remedy.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a server-level /library/create test posting a code-review project LLM criterion (gate=code_review, exec=1-TURN) with empty/missing/blank/non-list applies_to that asserts a 400 with the `use ["**"]` remedy AND that no rubric or criteria_routing.json overlay was written.
evidence: editor_server.py:382-390 wires the new guard: `errors = editor_contracts.validate_criterion_authoring(pid, routing)` then `if errors: self._send(400, ...); return` BEFORE `author_criterion(...)`

The only /library/create-with-routing server test uses a routing dict with NO `gate` key (test_editor.py:421-426: `{"exec": "1-TURN", "applies_at": {...}, "block_threshold": 0.95, "default_posture": "advisory"}`), so `validate_criterion_authoring` short-circuits at editor_contracts.py:260-261 `if routing.get("gate") != _CODE_GATE: return []` and the new refusal path is never taken.

validate_criterion_authoring is exercised only as a bare function in test_editor_batch.py:148-207, never through the HTTP handler; no assertion that the rubric/overlay file is absent after a refused save.
ABSENCE: a regression where _library_create omits the validate call, or writes the file before validating, would pass every existing test (the pure-function unit tests still return the right list).
blocking.finding: The fail-loud save guard (AC3) is verified only as a pure function; no test exercises /library/create refusing a code-review project LLM criterion with bad globs, so the server-seam wiring and the no-file-written-on-refusal contract are untested.
scenarios: A future refactor of _library_create drops or reorders the validate_criterion_authoring call, silently activating an invalid code-review project criterion.
The guard is present but author_criterion runs first, leaving a stranded rubric/overlay despite the 400.
blocking.suggested_fix: In tests/unit/workflow/test_editor.py, extend the /library/create suite with a case using routing={"gate": "code_review", "exec": "1-TURN", "default_posture": "advisory", "applies_to": []}; assert status==400, the remedy substring in body["errors"], and that .rebar/prompts/<sanitized>.md and .rebar/criteria_routing.json do not exist afterward.
